simple.meaning: שַׁחַל (shachal) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a lion (from his characteristic roar).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 4:10. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁחַל (H7826) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H7826. shachal שַׁ֫חַל noun masculine lion (poetry); — absolute ׳שׁ Hosea 5:14 +, שָׁ֑חַל Job 4:10 +; — lion , simile of ׳י , toward Israel Hosea 5:14 (|| כְּפִיר ), 13:7 (|| נָמֵר ); of guilty men Job 4:10 (|| כְּפִירִים אַרְיֵה, ); figurative of foes Psa 91:13 (|| כְּפִיר ) lion , as hunted 10:16 (in simile); literal Job 28:8 ; Prov 26:13 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root probably meaning to roar ;

occurrences.englishText: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion.
The proud animals have not trodden it,
You will tread on the lion and cobra.
The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road!
For I will be to Ephraim like a lion,
Therefore I am like a lion to them.
